citations.narrative:
- Multiple cages had sharp points near the water source for adult birds. Sharp points are a potential source of injury for the
enclosed animals, especially when located next to the source of drinking water. All sharp points within the cages should
be removed to protect the health and welfare of the enclosed animals.

- Multiple juvenile bird enclosures had inadequate space for the number of housed animals. Lack of adequate space may
result in a variety of negative effects on the birds, including stress, poor body condition, or abnormal behaviors. All
enclosures must be constructed and maintained to allow each contained bird to make normal postural and social
adjustments. Each bird must also be able to freely access feed and water, and escape aggression from other birds. The
licensee must ensure that the numbers of birds in each cage are appropriate for the size and type of cage being used.
This is a (1st) Re-License Inspection for a Class “A” license. The inspection and exit briefing were conducted with the
applicant.
All items must be in compliance within 2 more inspections or by 30 August 2026 or the applicant will forfeit the license fee
and must wait 6 months to reapply. Please contact your inspector to schedule your next Re-License Inspection.
Regulated activity can continue under your existing USDA license until it expires.
Additional Inspectors:
Sarah Roloff
CODY YAGER, Avian Field Specialist n
